content: Dexlansoprazole is indicated for the treatment and healing of all grades of erosive esophagitis (EE) and for maintaining the healing of EE. For healing, the recommended dose is 60 mg orally once daily for up to 8 weeks. For maintenance, the dose is 30 mg orally once daily for up to 6 months. It is also indicated for the treatment of heartburn associated with symptomatic non-erosive gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) at a dose of 30 mg orally once daily for 4 weeks. Dexlansoprazole interacts with various medications due to its effects on gastric pH and hepatic enzyme metabolism, particularly CYP2C19 and CYP3A4. These interactions can either increase or decrease the levels and effects of other drugs, potentially leading to reduced efficacy or increased toxicity. Below are specific interactions and recommendations: 1. Erlotinib: Concomitant use with proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) like dexlansoprazole should be avoided as it decreases erlotinib levels by altering gastric pH, reducing its solubility and bioavailability. 2. Mavacamten: Dexlansoprazole increases mavacamten levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism, which may lead to heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. Concomitant use is contraindicated. 3. Nelfinavir: Dexlansoprazole decreases nelfinavir levels, potentially leading to loss of virologic response and resistance. Concomitant use is contraindicated. 4. Rilpivirine: Dexlansoprazole reduces rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH, which may cause treatment failure and resistance. Concomitant use is contraindicated. 5. Acalabrutinib: Dexlansoprazole decreases acalabrutinib solubility and levels due to increased gastric pH. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Apalutamide: Apalutamide decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Atazanavir: Dexlansoprazole reduces atazanavir solubility and plasma concentrations. Avoid use in treatment-experienced patients. In treatment-naive patients, limit PPI dose to omeprazole 20 mg equivalent and administer 12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir. 8. Dasatinib: Dexlansoprazole decreases dasatinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Digoxin: Dexlansoprazole increases digoxin toxicity risk due to prolonged PPI use causing hypomagnesemia. Monitor closely. 10. Iron Supplements (e.g., ferrous sulfate, ferric gluconate): Dexlansoprazole decreases iron absorption by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor. 11. Methotrexate: Dexlansoprazole increases methotrexate levels by reducing renal clearance, increasing the risk of toxicity at higher doses. Monitor closely. 12. Clopidogrel: Dexlansoprazole reduces clopidogrel efficacy by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism, which is necessary for clopidogrel activation. Use caution and monitor platelet aggregation. 13. Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir: Dexlansoprazole decreases ledipasvir solubility and levels. If coadministration is necessary, use a PPI dose comparable to omeprazole 20 mg under fasted conditions. 14. Velpatasvir: Dexlansoprazole reduces velpatasvir solubility and levels. Avoid coadministration. If necessary, administer velpatasvir with food 4 hours before omeprazole 20 mg. 15. Midazolam: Dexlansoprazole increases midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially prolonging sedation. Monitor closely. 16. St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 17. Amphetamine/Dextroamphetamine: Monitor closely. 18. Bosutinib: Dexlansoprazole decreases bosutinib levels by approximately 45% due to pH-dependent solubility. Use caution and monitor. 19. Cannabidiol: Dexlansoprazole increases cannabidiol levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism, increasing the risk of adverse effects. Monitor closely and adjust doses as needed. 20. Mycophenolate: Dexlansoprazole decreases mycophenolate levels by increasing gastric pH, potentially reducing efficacy. This interaction is more significant with mycophenolate mofetil than with enteric-coated mycophenolate sodium. 21. Rifampin: Rifampin decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 22. Posaconazole: Dexlansoprazole decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. Monitor closely and consider alternative therapies. 23. Methyphenidate: Dexlansoprazole may alter the release characteristics of extended-release methylphenidate capsules due to pH-dependent dissolution. Monitor closely and consider separating administration times. 24. Mitotane: Mitotane decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust doses as needed. 25. Sotorasib: Dexlansoprazole decreases sotorasib levels by reducing gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid coadministration or adjust dosing intervals. 26. Tucatinib: Tucatinib increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or adjust doses as needed. 27. Diazepam: Dexlansoprazole increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism, potentially increasing adverse effects. Monitor closely. 28. Flibanserin: Dexlansoprazole increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of adverse effects. Monitor closely. 29. Gefitinib: Dexlansoprazole decreases gefitinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration if possible. If necessary, separate doses by 12 hours. 30. Lenacapavir: Lenacapavir increases dexlansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 31. Methotrexate: Dexlansoprazole increases methotrexate levels by reducing renal clearance, increasing the risk of toxicity at higher doses. Monitor closely. 32. Sparsentan: Dexlansoprazole decreases sparsentan levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism, potentially reducing efficacy. Monitor closely. 33. Fosamprenavir: Dexlansoprazole decreases fosamprenavir levels by increasing gastric pH. Monitor closely. 34. Belumosudil: Dexlansoprazole decreases belumosudil levels by increasing gastric pH. Increase belumosudil dosage to 200 mg twice daily when coadministered with PPIs. 35. Lemborexant: Dexlansoprazole increases lemborexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lower the lemborexant dose if coadministered. 36. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases dexlansoprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 37.
